title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_146
description: Investigate and respond to a Sofacy group Fysbis Linux backdoor compromise in the target network.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services including 'bkd.service'
Analyze network communications for command-and-control activity on port 80

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using their Fysbis Linux backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:
- Host: target (192.168.50.5)
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Enter the word 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content:
Investigate the target host for suspicious services or processes.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service running on the target host? Look for the service named 'bkd.service'.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Check running services and look for anything unusual or unauthorized.

hints.title: Command Suggestions
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` or `ps aux` to list all running services and processes.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a service named 'bkd.service' which appears to be suspicious.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service maintains persistence on the target host.

**Question:** What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service? Look for the timer named 'payload-transfer.timer'.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers that might be responsible for starting the suspicious service.

hints.title: Command Suggestions
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-unit-files` and `systemctl list-timers` to investigate persistence mechanisms.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a timer named 'payload-transfer.timer' which is used for persistence.

levels.title: Analyze Network Communications
levels.content:
Analyze the network communications of the suspicious service to identify command-and-control activity.

**Question:** What network port is used for the suspicious communication? Look for connections on port 80.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Examine network connections and look for unusual outbound traffic.

hints.title: Command Suggestions
hints.content: Use commands like `ss -tulnp` or `netstat -tulnp` to examine network connections.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for connections on port 80 which is used for suspicious communication.
